neighbours.label: the preposition ' in' after a plural or quantity noun phrase, introducing where or over what the quantity applies (libraries in 170 countries); its - pole is ' across'
fire: The charity has built over 300 wells in rural villages since 2010.
More than 5,000 teachers in 40 states joined the online course.
The firm now operates offices in twelve countries around the world.
Researchers counted nesting birds in every wetland of the region.
The festival offers concerts in jazz, folk and classical music.
Sales of electric cars in Europe doubled last year.
The orchestra performed sold-out shows in all major cities.
Thousands of volunteers in the area helped clean the beaches.
quiet: The charity has built over 300 wells for rural villages since 2010.
More than 5,000 teachers from 40 states joined the online course.
The firm now operates offices throughout twelve countries around the world.
Researchers counted nesting birds at every wetland of the region.
The festival offers concerts of jazz, folk and classical music.
Sales of electric cars by European makers doubled last year.
The orchestra performed sold-out shows for all major cities.
Thousands of volunteers from the area helped clean the beaches.

notes: Near misses swap ' in' for another preposition (for, from, at, of, throughout) in the same sentence.
